item.title: Ducks land in CFP rankings despite rocky season
item.description: Oregon football’s season hasn’t worked out the way it expected. But the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) were ranked in the first College Football Playoff rankings. Oregon came in at No. 23 in the initial rankings, revealed live on ESPN on Tuesday. Dan Lanning’s team is on the outside looking in at the 12-team playoff, one season before a 24-team playoff is set to likely go into effect. The No. 23 Ducks are coming off a confidence-boosting win over Northwestern, heading on the road to face No. 12 Ohio State (6-2, 4-1) this Saturday. That matchup originally included the preseason Nos. 1 and 2 teams in the AP poll. But in this chaotic college football season, the Buckeyes are reeling after a road loss to No. 20 USC. Other Big Ten teams in this week’s CFP rankings include No. 19 Iowa, No. 8 UCLA and No. 4 Indiana. item.title: Ravens’ Jesse Minter doesn’t hold back on ‘unacceptable’ play after latest blowout loss
item.description: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Ravens’ Jesse Minter doesn’t hold back on ‘unacceptable’ play after latest blowout loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens suffered a blowout 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football, extending their losing skid to four straight games. The Ravens started undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano amid their quarterback injury crisis, and he was unable to make much of an impact in the game after the Ravens went down big. While Ravens head coach Jesse Minter acknowledged the team was in a tough spot with Fagnano starting, he was not pleased with their second-half showing . “In the second half, we just got in our own way. We’re turning the ball over a couple times in a row. The defense was out there, it felt like the whole half. I thought they battled and fought, and did a decent job in the second half. But obviously, the results are not acceptable for us and what we’re after,” Minter said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After a relatively clean first half, Fagnano immediately threw an interception in the first drive of the second half, which led to a Jaguars field goal. The Ravens then committed back-to-back turnovers with another pick and a fumble to start the fourth quarter, which allowed the Jags to blow the game wide open. These second-half collapses are becoming a common occurrence for the Ravens. Their current four-game losing streak started with back-to-back meltdowns against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals with Tyler Huntley at quarterback. While the absence of Lamar Jackson amid this skid has been huge, Minter has much work to do in terms of keeping his team playing to a high standard for the entire game. item.title: Ilia Topuria Opens Up on Psychological Impact of Justin Gaethje Loss in First Interview Since UFC Freedom 250
item.description: Ilia Topuria’s UFC return is gaining momentum with each passing day. A couple of days ago, the former two-division champion visited his native Georgia, giving fans a glimpse of his recovery. More recently, he stopped by the iconic Didgori Battle Memorial on Mount Didgori, a site that symbolizes Georgian resilience and victory. Amid all this, Dana White also provided an important update on Topuria’s status , confirming that the Spaniard is expected to be ready to return in the first quarter of 2027. With contenders like Paddy Pimblett and Arman Tsarukyan , along with reigning champion Justin Gaethje, in the mix, it will be interesting to see what’s next for “El Matador.” “He’ll be back in ’27. We’re working on that too.” @DanaWhite confirms Ilia Topuria’s return to #UFC will happen next year. https://t.co/tbRDbrnMo4 — Jim Rome (@jimrome) November 4, 2026 ALSO READ: Dana White Gives Green Light to Alexander Volkanovski vs. Justin Gaethje Lightweight Title Fight, Reveals Potential Roadblock However, Topuria recently sat down for his first exclusive interview since his loss to Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 in June 2026. In a preview clip released by ABC Diario on Thursday, fans got a glimpse of the Spaniard’s mindset after suffering the first defeat of his professional career and falling to 17-1. He said, “I’ve been in the worst situation a fighter can possibly be in. I’ve experienced the worst day of my career. What’s worse than that? Dying?” Topuria also opened up about the psychological impact of the defeat, admitting that he had spent months questioning what went wrong. “Was something off is a question I’ve had to face over the last five or six months, but one thing is clear: you either win, or you lose; and I lost. If I wake up in the morning and look in the mirror and it was like, ‘No, no, no, no, no, this is not me.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by ABC (@abc_diario) This isn’t the first time Topuria has opened up about the loss. Back in September, he took to social media to reflect on the devastating defeat in a short video essay addressed to his son, Hugo. He offered an even deeper look into his experience following his first MMA defeat. The former double champion published a lengthy nine-part piece titled “This Is Me” on his website, taking readers through his entire journey in the sport. Topuria candidly revealed that he struggled to recognize his own face when he looked in the mirror the morning after his fight with Gaethje. He also disclosed that he suffered fractures to both orbital bones, a broken septum, and a broken foot during their brutal back-and-forth encounter. Of course, Topuria was eventually forced to retire on his stool at the end of the fourth round against Gaethje at the White House. Now, with his return potentially just months away, the big question is whether “El Matador” can rediscover the confidence that made him one of the UFC’s most feared fighters.

item.title: REPORT: Warsofsky’s Job Safe for Now
item.description: San Jose Sharks head coach Ryan Warsofsky isn’t on the hot seat yet. That’s what Pierre LeBrun reported on TSN’s Insider Trading on Thursday. “The Sharks are near the bottom in goals for. They’re near the bottom in goals against. It’s ugly. The team’s struggles have led to speculation about Ryan Warsofsky,” LeBrun said. “My understanding is that Sharks GM Mike Grier is not contemplating a coaching change at this stage.” The San Jose Sharks, after a 6-4-1 start, have slumped, losing five of their last six. They got stomped 7-2 at the Los Angeles Kings on Wednesday, leading to a players-only meeting. “It’s not on the coaches right now,” Kiefer Sherwood said afterwards. Warsofsky, going into the last year of his contract, signed a multi-year extension before the season. Warsofsky and his coaching staff, spearheaded by an MVP-caliber Macklin Celebrini campaign, had led a 34-point improvement in the standings last year. Grier followed that up in the off-season by committing over $100 million to veterans Mason Marchment , Darnell Nurse , Jacob Trouba, and Michael Kesselring, raising expectations for a San Jose playoff berth, which would be their first since 2019. But dragged down by mostly poor 5-on-5 play, along with injuries to glue center Alex Wennberg and top winger Igor Chernyshov, the Sharks have sputtered recently. It looks like Warsofsky will get some time to turn the San Jose Sharks around. But for how long? Related Headlines Sharks Insight: Does San Jose Need Different Voice Besides Warsofsky? item.title: ‘Bro, let me tell you’: Ayo Dosunmu shares what has shocked him about LaMelo Ball
item.description: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images LaMelo Ball is one of the most fun players to watch in the NBA. The Minnesota Timberwolves superstar has had an incredible start to the season, and some of the shots he has pulled off have been incredible to see. Ball’s teammate, Ayo Dosunmu, has now shed some light on what the 25-year-old is actually like behind the scenes. Ayo Dosunmu says he has never seen anyone like LaMelo Ball One of the first things people usually say about Ball is that he is ‘too chill’. Dosunmu has heard that several times, but he wants to tell everyone that his Minnesota Timberwolves teammate is actually very serious about the game. Despite being a superstar and worth an absolute fortune, Ball apparently asks more questions in practice than anyone else to improve his game. That seems to have surprised Dosunmu, as he had never seen anyone do the above. Speaking about people’s perception that “LaMelo is too chill,” he wrote in The Players’ Tribune : “Bro, let me tell you something about LaMelo. “He’s more curious about the game of basketball than anybody I’ve ever seen at his level. How many guys who are worth $300 million are still asking questions every day in practice? “He’s worth $300 million, and he’s trying to learn and get better every day.” That mentality is exactly what separates a good player from a great one, and it is no surprise to see Ball perform so well since the start of the season. With Anthony Edwards out injured, the Timberwolves need Ball to become more of a leader and deliver. So far, he has been doing that. item.title: ‘Wanting to win’: Justin Jefferson breaks silence on frustration with Vikings offense
item.description: Eric Hartline-USA TODAY Sports The Minnesota Vikings suffered their first loss of the season on Sunday, falling 19-15 to the Detroit Lions. And star wide receiver Justin Jefferson couldn’t hide his frustration, as the Vikings’ passing game struggled once again. Now, Jefferson has finally addressed what was bothering him. Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Jefferson said his frustration came from “wanting to win,” and warned that the Vikings are “wasting” the talent they have on offense if they don’t start executing. Jefferson’s Frustration Jefferson made one of the most impressive catches of the season on Sunday, tipping a pass to himself for a 1-yard touchdown. But he finished with just five catches for 33 yards, as quarterback Kyler Murray missed him on several throws, including an interception right before halftime. Jefferson, a two-time winner of the Korey Stringer Good Guy Award for his cooperation with local media, didn’t speak to reporters after the game. But both Murray and head coach Kevin O’Connell acknowledged that he was frustrated. “Obviously he’s frustrated, and that’s understandable. He is who he is, and he has every right to the way he feels when he doesn’t get the ball. That’s on us to find a way to get him the ball,” Murray said, via ESPN’s Kevin Seifert . “These guys want to win. I don’t fault the frustration or the competitiveness in any way, shape or form,” O’Connell added. Despite the Vikings’ 6-1 start, Jefferson is off to the worst start of his career, with 28 catches for 335 yards this season. Minnesota’s offense also ranks near the bottom of the league in both points and yards per game. Making matters more complicated, Murray suffered a hamstring injury against the Lions and has been ruled out for Monday night’s game against the Buffalo Bills. Carson Wentz will start in his place. ‘Wanting to Win’ On Thursday, Jefferson spoke to reporters for the first time since the loss and explained where his frustration was coming from. “It was wanting to win, and I felt like we had plenty of opportunities to win that game and we only hurt ourselves in multiple ways. item.description: Nov 5, 2026; Tucson, Arizona, USA; Cal Poly Mustangs guard Guzman Vasilic (5) rebounds the ball while Arizona Wildcats guard Bryce James (6), Caleb Holt (3), and center Motiejus Krivas (13) attempt to steal it during the first half at McKale Center at ALKEME Arena. Mandatory Credit: Aryanna Frank-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Home is where the heart is. And almost always a win in November. Arizona cruised to a 104-84 victory over Cal Poly on Thursday night at ALKEME Arena at McKale Center in its home opener. It was the UA’s 52nd win in 53 November games at McKale since the 2012-13 season, the only loss coming two years ago to Duke. Motiejus Krivas scored a career-high 30 points, while Ivan Kharchenkov followed up his career-best 38 in the opener against UCLA with 16 along with 10 rebounds, seven assists and four steals. Caleb Holt had 21 points and eight rebounds and Cameron Holmes added 13. Arizona shot 54.5 overall, held Cal Poly to 43.9 percent shooting, were plus-14 on the boards and forced 19 turnovers with 14 steals. It was the most steals in three years. Cal Poly made 16 3-pointers on 37 attempts, eight from Hamad Mousa who went for 30. Krivas was 10 of 13 from the field after only taking four shots against UCLA’s constant double team. He still got fouled plenty and made 10 of 12 from the line, adding eight rebounds and two blocks. Holt made 8 of 13 shots and Holmes, who didn’t play in the second half of the opener after looking gun shy from the perimeter, was 5 of 9. Arizona led 59-41 at halftime, its most points in the 1 st half since scoring 61 in the 2023-24 opener against Morgan State. With a comfortable lead, the 2 nd half was more of an open run than a scripted attack, which led to some sloppy play on both ends. The lead dipped to 17 with 11:30 to go before the UA ripped off 12 in a row, with Krivas topping his previous high of 25 along the way. The run also featured Kharchenkov diving for a loose ball to call timeout with a 25-point lead, then after getting the whistle mugging to the crowd while still on the ground. Cal Poly was called for five fouls in the first 56 seconds, one on the offensive end, as Arizona jumped out to an 11-3 lead that included a 3 by Bryce James , who have five points, two assists, two steals and a rebound in 17 minutes. He wasn’t the first sub, like normal, with Maksim Brnovic and JJ Mandaquit coming in just before the under-16 timeout for Holt and Kharchenkov. The Mustangs twice got within one thanks to some Arizona turnovers but a 9-0 run created some breathing room, then a 13-0 run that included nine points from Holmes to make it 41-20. He hit an open 3, the kind he passed up on Monday, made a transition layup and then dunked off a steal and made a pull-up mid-range jumper. The UA had four players reach double figures before halftime, with Holmes getting there on a putback layup just before the buzzer. item.title: Ravens’ Jesse Minter declines to give any Lamar Jackson injury update after losing to Jaguars
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Ravens’ Jesse Minter declines to give any Lamar Jackson injury update after losing to Jaguars appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jacksonville Jaguars defeated the Baltimore Ravens 33-10 on Thursday night, extending the Ravens’ losing streak to four games . The Ravens were without quarterback Lamar Jackson , who had injured his right throwing thumb in a collision against the Buffalo Bills. Jackson was making a return from a Grade 1 high ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans, and may now be out for the season. Asked about his status, head coach Jesse Minter refused to comment , per a post on X by Luke Jones. “I’m not going to speak on that,” he said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The loss dropped the Ravens to 4-5, while Jacksonville improved to 6-2 with its fifth victory in six games. Jackson suffered the thumb injury on his first offensive snap against the Bills when he collided with rusher Greg Rousseau while attempting a pass to Zay Flowers. The Ravens lost that game 36-10, and Minter had previously confirmed that Jackson would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. item.title: Duke Crushes Coastal Carolina By 61
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 5: John Blackwell #13 of the Duke Blue Devils is fouled by Derrick Green #15 of the Coastal Carolina Chanticleers in the first half at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 5, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images C oastal Carolina came out Thursday night and quickly made it clear that this was going to be a physical game for Duke. In the first few minutes, the Chanticleers hammered Duke inside, and that continued for the whole game. Several players were in situations that could have resulted in injury. John Blackwell was thrown to the ground and grimaced in immediate pain. It looked much more serious than it was, fortunately. Ngongba got pushed backwards and hit the floor hard enough to make a noise that was heard throughout Cameron. Sebastian Wilkins got poked in the eye, which could have been quite serious. There was more, too. All it really seemed to do in the end, though, was to piss Duke off. After adjusting to what Coastal was trying to do, Duke shot out to a 16-0 lead, en route to a 113-52 win. The 61-point margin was the biggest of Jon Scheyer’s career. Pat Ngongba was particularly dominant, with a career-best 28 points. In fact, Duke and Ngongba were so dominant that he was personally outscoring Coastal Carolina until Trey Perry got the Chanticleers to 29 points with 11:33 to play. Duke’s offense was really impressive, and offense always gets the most attention, but the defense was tremendous. Coastal only shot 4-22 from deep (18 percent), and 19-63 (30 percent) overall, and a fair amount of that came after Duke eased up late. Coastal was outrebounded 53-27, and had 15 turnovers. Of those rebounds by Duke, 39 were defensive. Toss in the 17 turnovers, and that’s 56 potential shots Duke denied Coastal. Ross in 9 blocks, and that’s 65. The pressure was overwhelming, but it wasn’t just coming from defense. Duke’s offense put a lot of pressure on the Chanticleers as well. Ngongba shot 10-13/2-3, and that, alone, was almost impossible to overcome. He also had 9 rebounds. John Blackwell had 15, Dame Sarr had 12, Cayden Boozer 11, and JoJo Boumtje Boumtje had 9. Duke assisted on 25 of 38 shots, which works out to nearly 66 percent. And this is something truly impressive: Boozer had 12 assists to 1 turnover. The Blue Devils got 38 points from the bench, including 15 from Caleb Foster in just 17 minutes. Bryson Howard and Deron Rippey scored 8 each, including two breathtaking drives by Rippey. Cameron Williams got his first three-pointer, while Sebastian Wilkins scored 4, and also pulled down 11 rebounds to lead Duke in that category. Look at it this way: Ngongba, Boozer, and Wilkins each set a personal best in scoring, assists, and rebounds respectively, and Foster shot 5-7 off the bench. Consider this too: playing Coastal Carolina will probably serve them well as a warm-up for an always-physical Michigan State. Duke will see them Tuesday in Chicago. Notes – Drew Scharnow

item.title: Wisconsin stays unbeaten with tie plus shootout win at Minnesota
item.description: Top-ranked Wisconsin gave Minnesota senior goaltender Luca Di Pasquo all he could handle for 65 minutes only to take a tie out of the first matchup of the season for the border rivals Nov. 5 at 3M Arena at Mariucci in Minneapolis. For the purpose of records, the game goes down as a 1-1 tie. But after regulation and five minutes of three-on-three overtime, the Badgers’ Bruno Idžan found the net in a shootout to give the Badgers an extra point in the Big Ten standings . The game was a stark change for UW (6-0-1, 2-0-1 Big Ten) after a weekend in which it swept Notre Dame by scores of 7-1 and 9-1. Minnesota, ranked 18 th , went to 3-3-3 (1-0-2 Big Ten) with its third tie in nine games under first-year coach Brett Larson. The game was the first among three unconventional Thursday-Saturday sets the Badgers will play in the regular season. The completion scheduled for 7 p.m. Nov. 7 with streaming coverage on B1G+. UW pushed Di Pasquo to the limit Di Pasquo made 41 saves, including 16 in the second period, and four in overtime. Idžan, a sophomore from Croatia and the Badgers’ leading goal scorer, slipped a backhander around Di Pasquo on the first attempt in the shootout. On the subsequent tries, Gavin Morrissey lost the puck and Dylan Compton was denied by Di Pasquo. Wisconsin sophomore Alexis Cournoyer made 16 saves to earn his fourth win since transferring from Cornell. UW held the Golden Gophers to seven shots on goal after the first period. Wisconsin actually trailed The Badgers fell behind in a game for the first time this season when Mason Moe scored on the power play 10:19 into the opening period, resulting in the Badgers playing from behind for nearly 17 minutes. Grady Deering was in the box for the Badgers, serving a five-minute major for an illegal check to the back, a penalty that also resulted in the third-line center missing the rest of the game. Minnesota-born freshman Zach Wooten, playing on the top line with Morrissey and JJ Wiebusch, tied the game for UW with a shot from the slot 6:52 into the second period after taking a pass from Wiebusch behind the net. Wooten has scored points in five straight games with three goals and three assists. An honor for a Badger Earlier in the day, the U.S. Collegiate Selects announced that UW junior defenseman Logan Hensler, a 2025 Ottawa Senators first-round draft pick, will be a part of the team for the 2026 Spengler Cup in December in Switzerland. That means for the second straight year one of the Badgers’ top players will miss the Kwik Trip Holiday Face-off at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee, following Quinn Finley. The six-team Spengler Cup is the world’s oldest invitational hockey tournament, having started in 1923. item.title: Ronaldo’s Big Ego Made Him The Greatest Scorer Ever
item.description: Jul 6, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Portugal forward Cristiano Ronaldo (7) reacts after a Round of 16 match between Spain and Portugal in the 2026 FIFA World Cup at Dallas Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Let’s be honest about goalscorers. They need a big ego to do what they do, and Cristiano Ronaldo had the biggest of all. On Thursday, the 41-year-old legend told the world he is done playing for Portugal . He posted a long video message to announce the end of a career that spanned six World Cups. That is a lot of pressure for one man to carry, but he made it look easy. His decision came after a rough patch with coach Jorge Jesus . Tensions boiled over after Ronaldo was left unused against Norway despite warming up from half-time. He later said Jesus had broken an agreement on his minutes. When the coach then made clear he would not automatically start him against Denmark, Ronaldo left the training camp. That dispute proved to be the final break. Per Fox Sports , he said the day had come to hand back the famous No. 7 shirt. He claimed he never felt the shirt belonged to him alone, yet he wore it with a pride that felt like it did. The Heart of a Fighter Some folks think his drive was just natural talent. I say it was pure discipline mixed with a need to be the best. He grew up poor in Madeira, sharing a room with three siblings. His father struggled with alcohol, and Ronaldo once got expelled from school for throwing a chair at a teacher. He even had heart surgery when he was just 15. That kind of background builds a tough skin. He chased perfection in a way that seemed almost scary. While Lionel Messi played with a quiet focus, Ronaldo wanted to be a force of nature. He trained harder than anyone else and ate like a machine. Per Fox Sports, his 146 goals for Portugal were gigantic statements. Even his penalties felt like a victory lap. That celebration with the “SIUUUU” shout is just an exaggerated expression of “si,” which means yes in Spanish and Portuguese. It is an acceptance of grandiosity that only a true superstar can pull off. A Legacy That Stands Alone The Portuguese soccer federation released a statement full of nice words. They said they held “deep gratitude and immense admiration” for his service. They called his career immense and planned a fitting tribute. Before he arrived, Portugal had never won a major trophy. Now they have a European title and two Nations League wins. Ronaldo will keep playing club ball for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. He is chasing his 1,000th career goal and currently sits on 985.

item.title: DeWitt volleyball captures fifth consecutive district title
item.description: GRAND LEDGE - The DeWitt volleyball program has been a model of consistency over the years, making regional runs for four straight seasons while being one of the top teams in the Lansing area. During those runs have come district titles, and the Panthers have squared off with Grand Ledge in the district finals for four consecutive years. It was no different on Nov. 5, where the Comets once again stood in DeWitt's way. After sweeping Grand Ledge in both meetings in the regular season, the Panthers made it a clean 9-0 victory on the year, winning the district final in straight sets to claim the program's fifth district title in a row. "They showed a lot of composure tonight, and we're a real young team, but I was really impressed with the way we finished towards the end of the sets two and three," DeWitt coach Carley Robertson said. "The excellence of the DeWitt volleyball program started long before me, and there have been some really disciplined players come through this program. "They built something that people really wanted to be a part of, and we've been able to continue that forward and make it our own a little bit," Robertson added. "We've focused on the community aspect of wanting to be part of something, and that's a really positive experience for the kids." The Panthers controlled play in the first set, then finished off with 25-22 and 25-19 victories to complete the sweep. DeWitt will move on to the regional semifinals and will face Byron Center (38-5-2) on Nov. 10 at 5 pm at Richard Gull Lake High School. San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is reportedly inching closer to making a return to the NFL, after last having played in October 2024. Aiyuk suffered a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus injuries in his right knee against the Kansas City Chiefs, and now plans to return to the 49ers’ training facility. And well, tight end George Kittle hilariously declined to discuss Aiyuk’s potential return to the team, per a post on X by Grant Cohn. Kittle’s response came as Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, confirmed Wednesday that the 28-year-old had submitted the necessary paperwork to return and planned to report to the 49ers’ facility Friday afternoon. Rosenhaus said Aiyuk was healthy and ready to play, and San Francisco will now determine whether to reinstate Aiyuk.
